general_world_news.title: 🌍 World News
general_world_news.content:
• **United States-China:** Chinese President Xi Jinping will undertake a state visit to the United States from September 23 to 25, 2026, at the invitation of U.S. President Donald Trump. During the visit, the leaders are scheduled to hold in-depth discussions on major issues concerning China-U.S. relations and global peace and development. This meeting follows ongoing economic and trade consultations between the two countries, with negotiators reportedly working towards reducing tariffs on approximately $30 billion of goods from each nation. The summit aims to de-escalate trade friction and maintain a controlled détente, but long-term strategic competition over technology and influence persists.

• **United States-Iran Sanctions:** U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced on Monday, September 21, 2026, that all Iranian commercial airlines will cease global operations beginning Wednesday, September 23, 2026. This measure imposes broad secondary sanctions designed to isolate Tehran's civil aviation network, with international airports and entities servicing Iranian planes facing complete exclusion from the American banking system. Foreign operators will be prohibited from refueling aircraft, providing landing facilities, or selling passenger tickets without risking their access to dollar clearing. This action significantly escalates economic pressure on Iran, impacting its connectivity and commercial activities worldwide.

• **Ukraine-Russia Conflict:** Ukraine launched a massive drone attack into Russia over the weekend, with Moscow's mayor describing it as the biggest drone assault on the capital since the war began, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirming hits on a key oil facility and a military supply depot. Amidst these strikes, President Zelenskyy has emphasized Ukraine's readiness for an energy ceasefire with Russia and is scheduled to meet U.S. President Donald Trump on September 22, 2026, on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly session to discuss this potential de-escalation. The attacks and subsequent ceasefire discussions highlight the ongoing volatility and potential for significant shifts in the conflict's energy infrastructure targeting.

• **United Nations General Assembly:** The 81st session of the UN General Assembly's high-level general debate commenced on Tuesday, September 22, 2026, in New York City, under the theme "Restoring trust, managing transformation: a United Nations that delivers for all." World leaders, including U.S. President Donald Trump, French President Emmanuel Macron, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, are convening to address pressing global issues. This annual gathering serves as a critical platform for multilateral diplomacy, allowing leaders to shape international policy and coordinate responses to global challenges.

• **Global Economy/Inflation:** The International Monetary Fund (IMF) reported on September 21, 2026, that the world economy continues to face substantial risks from persistent inflation, elevated debt service costs, and artificial intelligence investment, though it has demonstrated greater resilience than initially anticipated. The ongoing conflict in the Middle East has emerged as a significant shock, contributing to an approximately 40% rise in Brent crude prices to around $107 per barrel as of September 14, 2026, and driving upward revisions in inflation forecasts for both the euro area (to 3.0% for 2026) and the United States (to 3.4% for 2026). This combination of geopolitical instability and inflationary pressures underscores the fragility of global economic recovery and the challenges central banks face in maintaining price stability.

Why it matters: The confluence of major power diplomacy, escalating economic sanctions, and continued regional conflicts, coupled with persistent global inflationary pressures, suggests a highly complex and interconnected global environment characterized by both efforts towards de-escalation and ongoing strategic competition.

eu_policy.title: 🇪🇺 European Union Policy
eu_policy.content:
• **Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/1221 amending Regulation (EU) No 575/2013 (Capital Requirements Regulation or CRR):** Previously: Institutions faced a uniform approach for calculating own funds requirements for market risk. Now: The regulation introduces temporary targeted operational relief measures and targeted multipliers for the calculation of an institution's own funds requirements for market risk, including for the profit and loss attribution test for trading desks using the alternative internal model approach. This provides flexibility for financial institutions. This offers financial institutions across the EU, including those in Portugal, temporary relief in managing market risk capital requirements, potentially optimizing capital allocation. Slaughter and May

• **Commission Delegated Regulation amending Annex I of Regulation (EU) 2021/821 (EU's dual-use export control list):** Previously: The export of certain emerging and strategically significant technologies might not have been subject to specific EU dual-use controls. Now: The update adds new controls on several technology clusters, including semiconductor manufacturing and testing equipment, advanced computing integrated circuits and electronic assemblies, ceramic matrix composites reinforced with mullite, rotary encoders based on inductive sensing technology, and additive manufacturing equipment for energetic materials. Businesses must now ensure compliance with updated export licensing requirements for these items. Businesses in the EU, including Portuguese exporters in high-tech manufacturing and R&D sectors, will face new obligations to screen their products against an expanded control list for exports outside the EU. The European Commission Updates the EU Dual-Use Export Control List

• **The European Union (Empowering Consumers for the Green Transition) Regulations 2026 (transposing Directive (EU) 2024/825):** Previously: Businesses could use generic environmental claims (e.g., "green," "eco-friendly") and claims based on carbon offsetting more broadly without strict verification. Now: The regulations, coming into operation on September 27, 2026, explicitly prohibit generic environmental claims unless the trader demonstrates recognized excellent environmental performance (e.g., EU Ecolabel or equivalent ISO 14024 Type I ecolabel). Claims of neutral, reduced, or positive environmental impact relying on carbon offsetting are also prohibited. All sustainability labels must be verified by a third party. This imposes stringent requirements on all EU businesses, including Portuguese companies, regarding environmental marketing claims and sustainability labelling, aiming to combat greenwashing and provide clearer information to consumers. McCann FitzGerald LLP

• **Cyber Resilience Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/2847) - Partial Application:** Previously: Manufacturers of products with digital elements lacked harmonized EU-wide mandatory reporting for cybersecurity incidents and vulnerabilities. Now: From September 11, 2026, manufacturers of products with digital elements (software and connected devices) must report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe security incidents to relevant authorities. An early warning is required within 24 hours of awareness, a detailed notification within 72 hours, and a final report within 14 days of a corrective measure or one month for severe incidents. This creates immediate and time-sensitive cybersecurity reporting obligations for all manufacturers of digital products operating in the EU, including Portuguese tech companies, enhancing supply chain security and consumer protection. Bird & Bird, Entry into force or application of EU legislation: key milestones

• **Data Act (Regulation (EU) 2023/2854) - Partial Application:** Previously: There was no explicit EU-wide requirement for connected products to be designed for user data access by default. Now: From September 12, 2026, connected products and related services placed on the market must be designed so that relevant data are, by default, easily, securely, and directly accessible to users free of charge, where relevant and technically feasible. This imposes a significant design and data management obligation on manufacturers of smart devices, IoT products, and connected services across the EU, including Portuguese businesses, granting users greater control over their generated data. Entry into force or application of EU legislation: key milestones, Wilson Sonsini

Why it matters: This week marks the operationalization of key digital and environmental regulations, demanding immediate compliance from businesses on cybersecurity incident reporting, data access design for connected products, and stricter substantiation for green claims, while also adjusting financial market capital requirements and expanding export controls on critical technologies.

portugal_policy.title: 🇵🇹 Portugal Policy & Law
portugal_policy.content:
Here is your PORTUGAL POLICY & LAW briefing for today, Tuesday, September 22, 2026:

• **Suplemento Extraordinário para Pensionistas:** O Governo aprovou, em Conselho de Ministros, a atribuição de um suplemento extraordinário e pontual para pensionistas em 2026. Anteriormente, não havia um suplemento específico para 2026 aprovado, embora estivesse previsto no Orçamento do Estado. Agora, os pensionistas com pensões de montante igual ou inferior a 537,13 euros receberão um suplemento de 200 euros; aqueles com pensões superiores a 537,13 euros, mas iguais ou inferiores a 1.074,26 euros, receberão 150 euros; e os beneficiários com pensões superiores a 1.074,26 euros, mas iguais ou inferiores a 1.611,13 euros, terão direito a 100 euros. Pensionistas com valores superiores a 1.611,13 euros não receberão este apoio. Este suplemento será pago em dezembro, juntamente com a pensão e o subsídio de Natal. O impacto prático é um reforço financeiro pontual para cerca de dois milhões de pensionistas com rendimentos mais baixos no final do ano.

• **Prorrogação do Regime Temporário de Redução do ISP:** O Conselho de Ministros aprovou a extensão do regime temporário de redução do Imposto sobre os Produtos Petrolíferos (ISP) aplicável à gasolina e ao gasóleo. Anteriormente, o regime temporário de redução do ISP tinha um prazo de validade. Agora, esta medida será prolongada até 31 de dezembro de 2026. O impacto prático é a continuidade da mitigação do impacto do aumento dos preços dos combustíveis para consumidores e empresas até ao final do ano.

• **Alargamento do Passe Ferroviário Verde:** O Governo aprovou um Decreto-Lei que alarga a aplicação do Passe Ferroviário Verde aos serviços urbanos de Lisboa e Porto. Anteriormente, o Passe Ferroviário Verde não abrangia os serviços urbanos destas áreas metropolitanas, exigindo a aquisição de diferentes títulos de transporte. Agora, o Passe Verde passa a ter âmbito nacional, cessando a necessidade de adquirir diferentes títulos de transporte ferroviário para quem se desloca a partir das áreas metropolitanas. O impacto prático é uma maior conveniência e integração para os utilizadores de transportes públicos ferroviários nas grandes cidades.

• **Lei sobre Ocultação do Rosto em Espaços Públicos:** Uma nova lei que estabelece sanções para quem obrigue alguém a ocultar o rosto entrará em vigor. Anteriormente, não existia uma legislação específica a abordar a coação para ocultação do rosto em espaços públicos. Agora, a partir de 23 de setembro de 2026, quem obrigar alguém a ocultar o rosto enfrenta multa ou até prisão. O impacto prático é a proteção das liberdades individuais e a promoção da segurança pública, criminalizando atos de coação.

• **Novas Regras para as Tarifas de Táxi no Regime TVDE:** Novas regras relativas às tarifas de táxi, integradas nas alterações ao regime jurídico do Transporte Remunerado de Passageiros em Veículos Disponíveis por Via Eletrónica (TVDE), entrarão em vigor. Anteriormente, o setor dos táxis e o TVDE operavam sob regimes mais distintos, com regras de tarifas separadas. Agora, a partir de 1 de outubro de 2026, os táxis poderão ser registados para a atividade de TVDE, desde que cumpram os requisitos aplicáveis, e as suas tarifas serão ajustadas de acordo com o novo regime. O impacto prático é uma potencial alteração na oferta e nos preços dos serviços de transporte de passageiros, aumentando a concorrência e flexibilidade para os consumidores.

Why it matters: As medidas mais significativas para cidadãos e empresas são a extensão do subsídio extraordinário para pensionistas, que proporciona um alívio financeiro direto, e a prorrogação da redução do ISP, que mantém os custos dos combustíveis controlados.
